newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle makes Chase pension custodian.
newsitem.headline: Nestle makes Chase pension custodian.

text.p: Nestle SA said that it had named Chase Manhattan Corp as a custodian for a small portion of its pension assets which are being pooled from some of the concern's holdings in several different countries.
Jean-Pierre Steiner, vice president of Nestle's pension fund department, told Reuters in a telephone interview that the move was unusual in that assets of several Nestle units were pooled.

"It is related to a tentative project that we have tried to set up with the other Nestle funds of the group, and something that we have thought Chase would be best suited to run as custodian," Steiner said.
He said the move was aimed at creating larger concentrations of assets which would allow them more investment leeway.
"We'll just to try to get some synergy in managing the various Nestle fund assets," Steiner said.
He said the move is "taking into account that some funds are small or medium-sized, and cannot invest properly in international markets by themselves due to the sheer size of their assets."
Some Nestle pension funds, including those of Switzerland and the U.S. and the U.K., already had a global custodian.
Steiner said the assets involved were less than five percent of the total assets.
He said the transfer of those assets to Chase as custodian was done at the end of 1996.

Investment sources say that custodianship has become a competitive business, evolving from what previously was a simple caretaker role to a more active job involving performance measurement and other duties. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
